text:
priya: quick q — when streaming NDJSON structured outputs, should we emit optional fields as "key: null" or just omit the key? hitting inconsistent client behaviour across JS/Rust/mobile SDKs

Dan: prefer omit for optional/empty fields. 
priya: curious why?

Dan: because typed clients map missing -> undefined/Option::None which is usually safer than forcing a null value that some languages/libraries treat as a present-but-empty value. null has semantic meaning (explicitly null) whereas absent typically implies no value.

maria: fwiw some older mobile json mappers will throw if a key is missing and a model field is non-optional. Are we changing client SDKs to be defensive?

Dan: agree we should be defensive. two parts: 1) server contract: document that optional fields are omitted when empty, not null. 2) SDK guidance: generated models should treat fields as optional and handle missing keys gracefully. we'll provide migration notes.

priya: proposal for validators: JSON Schema for the API should NOT mark those optional fields as "nullable" unless we intend to return explicit null. Instead mark them as optional (i.e., not required). That way schema validation accepts absent but rejects an unexpected null if we didn't design for it.

Dan: exactly. and for streaming specifically (Content-Type: application/x-ndjson) each line is a complete JSON object. parsers: line -> JSON.parse (js) or serde_json::from_str (rust). both will give you null vs absent differences at runtime so test clients accordingly.

priya: small example for node parsing we can paste in docs:

```
// NDJSON line example
const line = '{"id":"1","choices":[{"text":"hi","metadata":null}]}';
const obj = JSON.parse(line);
console.log(obj.choices[0].metadata); // null vs undefined if omitted
```

maria: and rust snippet for devs:

```
// serde example
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Choice {
  text: String,
  metadata: Option<Metadata>,
}
let c: Choice = serde_json::from_str(line)?; // metadata == None when missing or null maps to None too unless using Option<Option<T>>
```

priya: good call about Option<Option<T>> — if we need to distinguish explicit null vs absent we should use nested option but avoid that unless necessary.

sdk-bot: note: existing TS SDK maps missing -> undefined, null -> null. Rust SDK maps both to Option::None by default unless using serde's preserve_null/explicit options.

priya: action: I'll update API docs with a clear rule: "optional fields are omitted when empty; explicit nulls are only used when documented as meaningful". also adding a short compatibility section for client teams and a canary flag.

Dan: canary plan sounds good. also add a linter rule to our contract tests: reject explicit null in responses for those optional fields unless the schema allows nullable.

maria: pinging mobile owners to audit deserializers.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for api/v2/streaming-contract-updates — 5% canary in eu-west1. :rocket:

priya: thanks — i'll draft the doc and open a small PR. cc @dan for the contract-test rule. :thumbsup:

Dan: thx, will review.
